newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to probe alleged cartel in steel sector.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to probe alleged cartel in steel sector.

text.p: The Brazilian government has opened a probe into the steel, aluminum and pharmaceutical sectors to investigate allegations of price-setting and excessive prices increases, an official said.

The decision was taken by the Justice Ministry's Economic Law department which ordered steelmakers Cosipa, CSN and Usiminas to suspend a price hike of between four and 12 percent they had planned to implement late June, the official at the ministry said.
The department is investigating whether the companies formed a cartel to set prices.
The Justice Ministry's department also ordered Hoescht Marion Roussel, a unit of pharmaceutical group Hoescht AG, to revoke increases in drug prices of up to over 50 percent since early this year.
The government is also probing eight aluminum sulphate firms which allegedly increased their prices excessively in 1994.
The companies will have to pay a daily fine of up to 55,000 reais if they do not suspend the price increases, the official said.
The steelmakers had no comment on the government's decision to block the planned price increase.
Spokesmen for CSN and Usiminas said the companies could not immediately comment on the issue because they had not yet been notified of the decision.
"For the time being, the company will not make any comment because it has not received any official statement (from the government)," a CSN spokeswoman said.
Cosipa also declined comment.
A spokeswoman for the Justice Ministry's deparment said all the companies would be notified of the probe Monday.
No officials at Hoescht Marion Roussel were immediately available for comment.
An official at the Brazilian Steel Institute (IBS) said he was surprised at the government's decision to open an investigation into the sector.
"We recently had a meeting with government officials and, at that meeting, they had decided to ask for further information. That decision took us by surprise," IBS director Marco Polo said.
Polo said the institute rejects the allegations that the companies formed a cartel to fix prices.

He said the steel firms announced different price levels and at different times. But he added that the companies announced similar percentage increases because they have "the same production structure."
The IBS director also criticized autoparts firms unions which, he said, are heading the allegations of price-setting in an attempt to delay or avoid the price increase.
Stocks of steel firms were lower midafternoon on the Sao Paulo bolsa following the news.
CSN shares dived 4.66 percent to 34.80 reais, Cosipa preferred lost 1.75 percent to 0.56 reais, while Usiminas fell 3.64 percent to 1.06 reais.
((-- Fatima Cristina, Sao Paulo newsroom 5511 2485412))
